questions.question: Describe how reverse bias at the gate controls the drain current in JFET. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how reverse bias at the gate controls the drain current in JFET.
  • i. No Gate V oltage (VGS = 0),The channel width is maximum and maximum current flows.
  • (0.5 Mark)
  • ii. When reverse bias is applied, the depletion region widens and channel width reduces.
  • Hence, drain current decreases. (1 Mark)
  • iii. Increasing Reverse Bias Further, reduces the channel width and drain current becomes
  • very small. (1 Mark)
  • iv. At a certain negative gate voltage, the channel is completely closed and drain current
  • becomes zero. (0.5 Mark)
  • v. Schematic diagram – 2 Marks
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the effect of positive and negative gate voltage on depletion MOSFET operation. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the effect of positive and negative gate voltage on depletion MOSFET operation.
  • D-MOSFET can operate in both depletion and enhancement modes, depending on whether
  • the gate voltage (VGS) is negative or positive. (1 Mark)
  • Depletion Mode-Applying negative voltage to the gate, Repels electrons from the channel.
  • Channel becomes narrower. Drain current decreases. (1 Mark)
  • Enhancement Mode-Applying positive voltage to the gate. Channel becomes wider and more
  • conductive. Drain current increases. (1 Mark)
  • Schematic Diagrams- 2 Marks
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Add 34 and 89 after converting to binary equivalent. Check your answer in decimal system. / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Add 34 and 89 after converting to binary equivalent. Check your answer in decimal system.
  • Convert to Binary- 2 Marks
  • 34 = 1000102
  • 89 = 10110012
  • Add the Binary digits – gives 11110112 - 2 Mark
  • Convert Result to Decimal-11110112=64+32+16+8+2+1=123- 1 Mark

questions.question: What are monolithic ICs? Explain the fabrication of transistors and capacitors in a monolithic IC. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What are monolithic ICs? Explain the fabrication of transistors and capacitors in a monolithic IC.
  • Monolithic ICs are integrated circuits in which all components (transistors, resistors, capacitors,
  • etc.) are fabricated on a single silicon chip. (1 Mark)
  • Transistor Fabrication
  • Diffusion in n-type epitaxial layer on p-substrate, SiO₂ etched for selective regions
  • Forms emitter, base and collector, metal contacts added (2 Marks)
  • Capacitor Fabrication
  • Formed using reverse biased P–N junction, P and N regions → plates, depletion region →
  • dielectric (2 Marks)
